name: S&P 500 cross-sectional momentum, thirty names
tier_label: returns, positions and a re-runnable strategy
suite_question: Is the measured edge real, and is the backtest that measured it trustworthy?
not_tested: Ticker identity for 52 name(s) (AAL, AMD, AMP, AN, BR, CBE): they hold more than one membership spell, and with no permanent identifier in the list a re-listing cannot be told from a symbol reused by a different company. Add an `id` column to resolve them.

Size of the survivorship bias: the membership list says which names were excluded, not what their returns would have been, so the count bounds how much is missing and not how much the result is overstated. That needs prices for delisted instruments.

Matched-exposure random-entry test: the position series is multi-asset. This test asks whether a single instrument was timed well, and reordering a cross-sectional book in time does not answer that question.

findings.title: Returns are explained by factor exposure
findings.detail: The returns are explained by exposures you can buy directly: alpha is 0.08% a year with a t-statistic of 0.03 (p=0.973) and the factors explain 72% of the variance; correlation to SPY is 0.82 and the strategy adds -0.027 annualised Sharpe over simply holding it at 1.04x leverage.
findings.remediation: Hedge the factor exposures and re-test the residual, which is the only part that could be alpha.

findings.title: Universe built from current index membership
findings.detail: Measured against the membership list: every name that left the index during the window is absent from it (AABA, AAL, AAP, ABC, ABMD, ACS, ADS, ADT, and 302 more). The backtest could not have chosen them, and they are the names most likely to have done badly - that is what leaving the index usually means. This counts how many names were excluded, not what their returns would have been, so it bounds the extent of the bias and not its size.
findings.remediation: Use a point-in-time constituent list. Where none is available, say so and treat the result as an upper bound. Supplying one to `data.membership_frame` replaces the declaration with a count.

data.universe_note: Thirty large, liquid names taken from present-day S&P 500 membership, each of which has been in the index continuously since before the sample starts. Assembled in 2026 from a screener, which is exactly how the bias gets in.
data.survivorship_basis_reason: measured against S&P 500 (fja05680/sp500 (MIT), reconstructed from index change announcements)

membership.source: S&P 500 (fja05680/sp500 (MIT), reconstructed from index change announcements)

sharpe.autocorrelation_note: annualising to 252 periods implies a sum over 251 lags, but 3773 observations can only speak to about 67; the adjustment assumes no dependence beyond that, and cannot rule out longer-horizon persistence

risk.note: block resampling with a mean block of 35.2 periods cannot reassemble drawdowns that unfolded over much longer horizons, so the resampled distribution understates how deep a drawdown this strategy can produce

selection.basis_note: Deflation runs on returns net of 5 bps, the upper end of realistic cost for US large-cap equities, so this figure sits slightly below the gross Sharpe in the headline.

null_max.method: stationary bootstrap of demeaned trials, rows resampled jointly

regimes.note: 63 leading observations had too little history to classify and are excluded

sign_flip.description: signs of 21-period blocks randomly flipped, preserving volatility clustering

perturbation.clean_claim: No dependence on data more than about 21 periods after the decision point. The strategy revises its position every 21 periods on average, and a leak shorter than that is overwritten before it reaches the book.
